messages:
sam: quick sanity check — hitting socket exhaustion in staging when we stream large responses + have Polly retry on transient faults. any obvious mistakes?

sam: using IHttpClientFactory named client, PolicyWrap with WaitAndRetryAsync(3). handler has PooledConnectionLifetime=2m, MaxConnectionsPerServer=50. code snippet:
```csharp
services.AddHttpClient(\"redwood\")
  .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler { PooledConnectionLifetime = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2), MaxConnectionsPerServer = 50 })
  .AddPolicyHandler(HttpPolicyExtensions.HandleTransientHttpError()
     .WaitAndRetryAsync(3, retryAttempt => TimeSpan.FromSeconds(Math.Pow(2, retryAttempt))));
```

sam: client calls look like:
```csharp
var resp = await client.GetAsync(url); // currently not using ResponseHeadersRead
await using var ms = new MemoryStream();
await resp.Content.CopyToAsync(ms); // streaming a lot of data
```

lina: two quick things — definitely use HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead when you want to stream. otherwise the whole body gets buffered and the connection stays tied up until content is read and disposed. also make sure you dispose the HttpResponseMessage and the stream. e.g.:
```csharp
using var resp = await client.GetAsync(url, HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead);
using var stream = await resp.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync();
await stream.CopyToAsync(target, 81920, ct);
```

lina: if Polly retries are wrapping the call, and the first attempt leaves the response undisposed, the retry will still cause new requests and you can run out of connections. ensure disposal happens even on cancellation/exceptions. :warning:

 t omas: also watch for synchronous blocking. don\'t .Result or .ReadToEnd on large streams — that holds threads and can hide connection leaks.

 t omas: consider moving the policy to the HttpMessageHandler pipeline so it only retries on transient network exceptions, not on long-running stream reads. e.g.:
```csharp
.AddPolicyHandler(HttpPolicyExtensions.HandleTransientHttpError().RetryAsync(2))
```

 t omas: if you need to abort streaming mid-way, call resp.Dispose() or cancel the token you passed to CopyToAsync. otherwise SocketsHttpHandler keeps the connection open until the connection is fully read/closed.

lina: also tune SocketsHttpHandler.MaxConnectionsPerServer + PooledConnectionIdleTimeout and consider PooledConnectionLifetime slightly higher than your typical request time. 2m might be OK but if your requests sometimes run for minutes, bump it. :mag:

sam: that makes sense. i missed ResponseHeadersRead and i was copying to MemoryStream which forced buffering. will switch to streaming copy and ensure using blocks.

sam: quick follow-up — should retry policy wrap the GetAsync call or the stream copy?

 t omas: only wrap the call that initiates the network operation. retries should cover transient network failures during request/response handshake. once you start streaming and partially read the body, retries are usually unsafe (idempotency). restructure so you retry before starting the stream, and if stream fails mid-read, treat as failure and surface it (maybe restart from application-level offset if supported).

lina: ping @sam when you push the PR and we\'ll run soak on staging. :thumbsup:

sam: pushed PR 1245 — changed to ResponseHeadersRead, disposed responses, and reduced buffering. will monitor connections. thanks!

infra-bot: deploy-notice: staging redeployed by @ci on 1851234601 — watch for increased ephemeral sockets over next 10m.

 sam: noted, will check graphs (TIME_WAIT, established) and report back.
